oneLine: Bitcoin and Ethereum fell 0.9–1.2% on October 25 as traders booked profits ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 28 decision, with market breadth skewed bearish and long positions crowded.
caveman: On Sunday October 25, Bitcoin dropped 0.9% and Ethereum dropped 1.2%. More contracts went down than up—about 55% lost value. People are holding a lot of long bets (making money if price goes up), and the funding payments traders pay each other were high, which shows everyone is bullish. But this is risky because if the price drops even a little, many traders lose at once. The big reason for the fall is that people were selling to lock in gains before the US Federal Reserve makes a big interest-rate announcement on Wednesday. It was a nervous, cautious day.
priceVolumeSummary: Bitcoin and Ethereum traded at tightly aligned prices across Binance, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, and Gate. Bitcoin volume dominated at $5.5 billion on Binance, with Ethereum at $4.8 billion; Binance set the pace on both.
positioningSummary: Bitcoin's open interest fell 2.4%, signaling liquidation of long positions despite a 2.2× long-to-short ratio on Binance—indicating aggressive longs among smaller traders but the largest traders (top position ratio: 1.70) hold less extreme bets. Funding rates stayed elevated at 10.95% annualized on BTC and 9.95% on ETH, rewarding short-sellers and penalizing buyers, a sign traders expect consolidation. Taker buy–sell ratios of 0.96 (BTC) and 0.91 (ETH) show more aggressive selling pressure than buying. Market breadth was bearish: 45.7% of Binance perps rose, while 54.3% fell—a net sell signal for sentiment.
stocksSummary: October 25 was a Sunday; Asian equity cash markets (Korea, Hong Kong, China) were closed. Commodity perps: gold up 0.31%, WTI crude down 0.67%, natural gas up 1.81%, copper up 0.75%.

topThree.headline: [Context, Oct 26] Anthropic files blockbuster IPO worth up to $100 billion; AI market sentiment spills into crypto.
topThree.what: The maker of Claude AI reported $16.3 billion in first-half revenue and $80.7 billion in net losses as it filed for a Nasdaq IPO. The announcement lifted tech sentiment and fueled speculation about AI infrastructure spending, which has knock-on effects on crypto mining and data-center demand.

topThree.headline: [Context, Oct 26] NBA joins CFTC prediction-market pact; crypto derivatives grow institutional traction.
topThree.what: The National Basketball Association signed a memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to enable prediction markets on games through venues like Kalshi and Polymarket. The deal signals regulator approval for crypto-native trading venues and reflects broader mainstream adoption.

topThree.headline: [Context, Oct 26] South Korea considers delaying crypto tax to 2029 as data-sharing with US stalls.
topThree.what: South Korea's government is mulling a fourth postponement of its cryptocurrency income tax from January 2027 to 2029, citing inability to obtain overseas trading data from US agencies until then. The delay removes a near-term regulatory headwind for Asian traders.

etfFlows.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted $443 million in net outflows on the last trading day before the report (Friday, Oct 23), as traders locked in gains ahead of the Federal Reserve's scheduled October 28 rate decision. Ethereum spot ETF flows for Oct 23 were not separately disclosed; however, ETH spot products recorded $1.61 billion in total outflows for October 2026, the largest monthly drain since July 2024 launch.

calendarNotes.event: Federal Reserve Rate Decision and FOMC Statement (Wed 28 Oct, 18:00 UTC)
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: Historically, crypto rallies on 'dovish' rate holds (no hike) and declines on surprise hikes or hawkish guidance. Oct 25 selling reflects traders unwinding longs before the announcement.

calendarNotes.event: US Advance GDP q/q, Core PCE, Initial Jobless Claims (Thu 29 Oct, 12:30 UTC)
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: Strong growth or inflation data can spook crypto; weak data may embolden rate-cut bets and lift sentiment.

glossary.definition: A payment between traders taking opposite sides of a perpetual futures contract. When funding is positive, buyers pay sellers every 8 hours (at Binance). Elevated rates signal optimism and can incentivize shorting if unsustainably high.

The number of traders holding long (bet on price rising) positions divided by those holding short positions. A ratio above 1 means more people are bullish; a ratio like 2.2 signals bullish leaning but also concentration risk.
The percentage of markets (cryptocurrencies or contracts) that moved up versus down in a given period. Breadth above 50% is bullish; below 50% is bearish.
The reference price used to calculate funding and liquidations on futures contracts. It is typically the average of recent trades across major venues, designed to prevent manipulation.
The total dollar value of all open (unrealized) futures positions in a market. Rising OI suggests fresh leverage entering; falling OI suggests positions are closing or being liquidated.
The percentage shift in total open positions over a period (e.g., a day). Negative change indicates net liquidation or position closure; positive indicates new margin entered.
The ratio of buy orders filled at ask (aggressive buying) to sell orders filled at bid (aggressive selling). Above 1 means more aggressive buying; below 1 means more aggressive selling.
The long-to-short ratio among the largest traders (those holding the biggest positions) on an exchange. It differs from the account ratio and can signal whether big players are aligned or hedging.
